sop_modules.name: Deck Protection & Furniture Staging
sop_modules.description: Mask siding at ledger board junction, deploy landscape and hardscape protection, stage deck furniture off work area, mask deck-mounted light fixtures. Identical protection requirements to NC deck spec.

tasks.name: Siding Protection at Ledger Board
tasks.description: Mask and tape siding adjacent to deck at ledger board junction. Tape at siding-to-deck transition, hang plastic 4-6 ft up siding face for spray_backbrush. Light tape for brush application.

quality_notes.all: Tape at siding-to-deck transition. For spray_backbrush, extend plastic 4-6 ft up siding to contain overspray.

tasks.name: Below-Deck Landscape Protection
tasks.description: Deploy plastic sheeting over plantings and landscape below elevated deck. Stain drips through board gaps.

quality_notes.all: Full coverage below deck footprint. Secure against wind.

tasks.name: Adjacent Hardscape Protection
tasks.description: Deploy canvas drop cloths and plastic over adjacent walkways, patios, and concrete at deck perimeter.

quality_notes.all: Canvas for crew traffic areas. Extend for spray overspray zone.

tasks.name: Deck Furniture Staging
tasks.description: Move deck furniture, planters, grills, and accessories off deck surface to staging area.

quality_notes.all: All items relocated. Clear working surface.

tasks.name: Deck Light Fixture Masking
tasks.description: Mask deck-mounted and railing-mounted light fixtures with tape and plastic bags.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage of fixture body and lens. Secure against wind.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Siding protection -> Landscape/hardscape protection -> Furniture staging -> Fixture masking.

sop_modules.name: Existing Coating Condition Assessment
sop_modules.description: RP-SPECIFIC MODULE. Mandatory assessment of existing coating condition before committing to prep strategy. Determines: (1) existing coating type via solvent test, (2) adhesion quality via ASTM D3359, (3) wood moisture content, (4) structural soundness via rot probe, (5) overall condition rating. Assessment results drive prep module activation and coating compatibility decisions.

tasks.name: Existing Coating Condition Assessment
tasks.description: Visual assessment of existing coating across all deck components. Rate condition as sound/worn/failing/peeling. Document wear patterns, adhesion failure areas, mildew, UV degradation. Identify high-traffic wear-through zones on floor. Check railings for coating loss at handrail contact points. Check stairs for tread wear-through.

quality_notes.all: Document condition per component. Photo-document wear patterns. Rate each component independently — floor may be peeling while railings are sound.

tasks.name: Existing Coating Type Identification
tasks.description: Identify existing coating chemistry: penetrating stain (oil or water-based), solid stain, or paint. Solvent wipe test: denatured alcohol dissolves latex/water-based, mineral spirits dissolve oil-based. Critical for coating compatibility determination — wrong product over wrong base causes adhesion failure.

quality_notes.all: Test minimum 3 locations per component. Document coating type. If unknown after testing, treat as incompatible — requires bonding primer or full strip.

tasks.name: ASTM D3359 Adhesion Test
tasks.description: Cross-hatch adhesion test on existing film-forming coatings (solid stain, paint). Score adhesion per ASTM D3359 scale (5B=perfect to 0B=complete failure). Minimum 3 test locations per component. Adhesion 3B or below triggers full strip. Penetrating stains do not form films — adhesion test not applicable for semi-transparent/semi-solid.

quality_notes.all: Document adhesion score per location. Adhesion <=3B = strip required. 4B = marginal — flag for estimator review. 5B = sound.

tasks.name: Deck Moisture Content Testing
tasks.description: Pin-type moisture meter readings across deck floor surface. MC >15% for PT pine or >12% for cedar/redwood is HARD STOP. Test shaded areas and end grain — read higher. Mandatory for all deck restain work.

quality_notes.all: Test minimum 5 locations. Include shaded areas. MC >15% = hard stop, do not proceed. Retest after 24 hr dry.

tasks.name: Rot Probe at Vulnerable Locations
tasks.description: Probe deck components at vulnerable locations with awl for soft rot: stair treads at nosing, post bases at grade contact, railing joints, board ends. Rot = HARD STOP for affected component — refer to carpenter for replacement before staining scope can proceed.

quality_notes.all: Probe all vulnerable joints. Document rot locations. Hard stop for affected component — not entire project.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Condition assessment -> Coating ID -> Adhesion test (film-forming only) -> Moisture test -> Rot probe. Assessment results determine which prep modules activate.

sop_modules.name: Deck Floor Prep for Restain
sop_modules.description: RP-specific floor prep: light scuff sand (sound existing), moderate sand with spot strip (worn), or full chemical strip (failing/peeling via chemical restore module). Pressure wash all conditions. Mildew treatment conditional.

tasks.name: Light Scuff Sand — Sound/Worn Existing Coating
tasks.description: Light scuff sand with 80-100 grit to degloss existing coating and promote adhesion for new stain. For sound existing: minimal material removal, just degloss. For worn: focus on wear-through edges to blend transition from bare wood to coated areas.

quality_notes.all: Uniform degloss across floor surface. Blend wear-through edges. No deep scratches — light pass only. Vacuum dust before washing.

tasks.name: Heavy Sand — Failing/Peeling Residual Coating
tasks.description: Aggressive sanding with 60-grit after chemical stripping to remove residual coating and smooth wood fiber raised by stripping process. Only activated when chemical restore module runs and leaves residual coating. Belt sander or random orbital.

quality_notes.all: Remove all residual coating. Smooth raised grain from chemical stripping. Sand WITH grain. Water drop test: immediate absorption.

tasks.name: Pressure Wash Deck Floor
tasks.description: Pressure wash deck floor at 1,000-1,500 PSI. Fan tip, maintain 12-18 inch distance. Removes dirt, mildew, sanding dust, and chemical residue. 24-48 hr dry time after (not included in rate). Always performed regardless of condition.

quality_notes.all: Fan tip only — never zero-degree on wood. Consistent overlapping passes WITH grain. 24-48 hr dry time minimum.

tasks.name: Mildew Eradication Treatment
tasks.description: Apply mildew treatment solution, dwell, scrub, rinse. Required when visible mildew present. Kill mildew spores before staining — stain over live mildew fails within one season.

quality_notes.all: All visible mildew eliminated. Rinse thoroughly — chemical residue inhibits stain adhesion.

tasks.name: Post-Wash Dry Verification
tasks.description: Verify deck surface has dried to acceptable MC after washing. Pin-type moisture meter check at multiple points. Confirm MC <=15% before stain application.

quality_notes.all: All test points below MC threshold. No visible wet spots. Surface ready for stain application.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Light sand (sound/worn) OR heavy sand after chemical strip (failing/peeling) -> Mildew treatment (conditional) -> Pressure wash -> 24-48 hr dry -> MC verify.

sop_modules.name: Railing and Spindle Prep for Restain
sop_modules.description: Hand sand and wash railing system and spindles. RP adds existing coating scuff/strip on railings. Activated when scope_components includes railings.

tasks.name: Railing System Sanding
tasks.description: Hand sand railing system (top rail, bottom rail, posts) per linear foot. Scuff sand existing coating for adhesion. For failing existing coating on railings, scrape loose material and feather-sand edges.

quality_notes.all: All railing surfaces sanded. Loose coating scraped and feather-sanded. Posts and rail undersides included.

tasks.name: Spindle/Baluster Sanding
tasks.description: Hand sand individual spindles — all 4 sides plus top/bottom transitions. Scuff existing coating. Turned spindles require profile-following with folded sandpaper.

quality_notes.all: All spindle surfaces sanded. Turned profiles followed. Existing coating scuffed for adhesion.

tasks.name: Railing System Wash
tasks.description: Wash railing system with garden hose or low-pressure wash. NOT high-pressure — protects detail profiles. Remove sanding dust and debris.

quality_notes.all: All surfaces clean. No sanding dust. Spindles rinsed. Allow dry time.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Railing sand -> Spindle sand -> Railing/spindle wash.

sop_modules.name: Chemical Restoration — Existing Coating Removal
sop_modules.description: 3-step chemical restoration for failing/peeling existing coatings: alkaline strip, acid brighten, rinse. Same protocol as NC weathered wood restoration. Requires separate mobilization day (24-48 hr dry time). RP activation: existing_coating_condition in [failing, peeling].

tasks.name: Chemical Stripper Application
tasks.description: Apply alkaline deck stripper by pump sprayer. Even coverage for uniform stripping. Work in manageable sections. For RP, may require stronger formulation for multi-layer existing coatings.

quality_notes.all: Even application. No dry spots. Working sections defined. Maintain wet edge.

tasks.name: Stripper Dwell Time
tasks.description: Allow chemical stripper to dwell per manufacturer spec. 15-20 min. Monitor for drying — re-wet if needed.

quality_notes.all: Dwell per manufacturer spec. Surface kept wet throughout. No premature drying.

tasks.name: Stripper Agitation/Scrub
tasks.description: Scrub stripper into surface with stiff bristle deck brush on pole. Agitates chemical into grain and loosens old coating. Labor-intensive.

quality_notes.all: All sections scrubbed uniformly. Old coating visibly loosening.

tasks.name: Stripper Rinse
tasks.description: Pressure rinse at 1,000-1,500 PSI to remove chemical residue and loosened coating. Thorough rinse critical — residual stripper prevents stain adhesion.

quality_notes.all: All chemical residue removed. Clean wood visible. Water runs clear.

tasks.name: Wood Brightener Application
tasks.description: Apply acid-based wood brightener by pump sprayer. Neutralizes alkaline stripper, restores natural wood color. Oxalic acid for cedar/redwood tannin management.

quality_notes.all: Even application. Wood color visibly brightening. No dry spots.

tasks.name: Brightener Dwell Time
tasks.description: Allow wood brightener to dwell per manufacturer spec. 10-15 min. Shorter dwell than stripper.

quality_notes.all: Dwell per spec. Uniform color change visible.

tasks.name: Brightener Rinse
tasks.description: Pressure rinse brightened surface. Remove all chemical residue. 24-48 hr dry time required before staining.

quality_notes.all: All brightener residue removed. Natural wood color restored. Surface pH neutral.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Strip apply -> Dwell -> Scrub -> Rinse -> Brighten apply -> Dwell -> Rinse -> 24-48 hr dry time -> RETURN VISIT for stain application.

sop_modules.name: Deck Floor Restain Application
sop_modules.description: Floor stain application — 4 method variants (spray_backbrush/brush/pad/roll) + conditional coat 2. Same application rates as NC once surface is prepped. Back-brushing mandatory for penetrating stains.

tasks.name: Floor Restain — Spray + Back-Brush (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Airless spray stain onto deck floor followed immediately by back-brushing to work stain into wood grain. 2-person crew. Back-brushing MANDATORY for penetrating stains.

quality_notes.all: Even penetration. No pooling between boards. Back-brushed within 30 sec of spray. Consistent color.

tasks.name: Floor Restain — Brush Application (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Brush-only stain application on deck floor. 4-inch stain brush, work with grain, maintain wet edge board-by-board.

quality_notes.all: Even penetration. No brush marks after absorption. Consistent color. Wet edge maintained.

tasks.name: Floor Restain — Pad Applicator (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Lamb's wool pad applicator on extension pole for deck floor. Good penetration with faster coverage than brush.

quality_notes.all: Even application. No pad marks after absorption. Wet edge maintained.

tasks.name: Floor Restain — Roller Application (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Roller application with 3/8-1/2 inch nap on extension pole. Best for solid stains where film-build matters more than penetration.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage. No roller marks after drying. No pooling between boards.

tasks.name: Floor Restain — Second Coat
tasks.description: Second coat uses same method as coat 1. Activated for all coating types on RP (weathered/stripped wood absorbs more, needs 2 coats for color build).

quality_notes.all: Even coverage over first coat. Consistent color depth. Maintain wet edge.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Coat 1 (selected method) -> Absorption/dry time -> Coat 2 (same method).

sop_modules.name: Railing and Spindle Restain Application
sop_modules.description: Railing stain (spray_backbrush or brush) + spindle stain (spray or brush) + coat 2 for each. Activated when scope includes railings.

tasks.name: Railing Restain — Spray + Back-Brush (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Spray stain on railing system followed by back-brushing. 2-person crew. All surfaces: top, sides, undersides of rails plus posts.

quality_notes.all: All railing surfaces coated. Posts fully coated. Back-brushed into grain. No runs on vertical faces.

tasks.name: Railing Restain — Brush Application (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Brush-only stain on railing system. 2-3 inch brush for rails and posts. Multiple surfaces per LF.

quality_notes.all: All surfaces coated. No brush marks after absorption. No runs.

tasks.name: Spindle Restain — Spray Application (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Spray stain on individual spindles — all 4 sides. Spray from multiple angles to coat all sides.

quality_notes.all: All 4 sides coated. No drips or runs. Even color.

tasks.name: Spindle Restain — Brush Application (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Brush stain on individual spindles — all 4 sides plus top/bottom transitions. 2-inch brush. Tedious hand work.

quality_notes.all: All surfaces coated including transitions. No drips.

tasks.name: Railing Restain — Second Coat
tasks.description: Second coat on railing system. Same rate and method as coat 1.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage over first coat. Consistent color depth. No runs.

tasks.name: Spindle Restain — Second Coat
tasks.description: Second coat on spindles. Same rate and method as coat 1.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage over first coat. Consistent color on all sides.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Railing coat 1 -> Spindle coat 1 -> Absorption time -> Railing coat 2 -> Spindle coat 2.

sop_modules.name: Deck Stair Restain Application
sop_modules.description: Stair step restaining — brush only, alternating step pattern for access. Activated when scope_components = full_deck.

tasks.name: Stair Step Restain — Brush (Coat 1)
tasks.description: Brush stain on individual stair steps (tread + riser per step). Alternating step pattern — stain every other step for access. End-grain sealing on exposed tread edges.

quality_notes.all: Full coverage on tread and riser. End grain sealed with extra coat. Alternating pattern maintained.

tasks.name: Stair Step Restain — Second Coat
tasks.description: Second coat on stair steps. Same alternating pattern. Same brush rate.

quality_notes.all: Even coverage over first coat. End grain fully sealed. Consistent color.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Coat 1 alternating steps -> Dry time -> Coat 2 remaining steps.

sop_modules.name: Final Inspection, Touch-Up & Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Final walkthrough inspection, touch-up staining, furniture return, protection teardown, tool cleanup.

tasks.name: Final Walkthrough Inspection
tasks.description: Walk entire deck inspecting for holidays, uneven color, missed spots, drips on railings. Check all components. Document solid stain delamination risk warning when coating_type=solid_stain.

quality_notes.all: Complete visual inspection. No missed spots. Color consistency verified.

tasks.name: Touch-Up Restaining
tasks.description: Brush touch-up of defects found during inspection. Spot re-stain holidays, even color variations, re-coat sanded drip areas.

quality_notes.all: All defects repaired. Touch-ups blended. No visible repair boundaries.

tasks.name: Furniture Return and Repositioning
tasks.description: Return all furniture, planters, grills to original positions. Verify surface is dry to touch before placing.

quality_notes.all: All items returned to original positions. No damage to fresh stain.

tasks.name: Protection Material Removal
tasks.description: Remove all protection materials — siding plastic, landscape tarps, hardscape covers, fixture bags. Check for tape residue.

quality_notes.all: All protection removed. No tape residue. No stain on protected surfaces.

tasks.name: Tool and Equipment Cleanup
tasks.description: Clean all staining equipment — flush sprayer, clean brushes/pads/rollers, dispose of used abrasives and chemical containers.

quality_notes.all: All tools cleaned. Sprayer flushed. Chemical containers disposed. Site debris removed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Final inspection -> Touch-up -> Furniture return -> Protection teardown -> Tool cleanup.
